hardDay.heading: Hard day? Start here.
hardDay.body:
Rest is real. Sabbath is a gift. If you're truly depleted, that isn't burial. Get help, sleep, heal, and let trusted believers carry you for a while.

Your task this week is honesty and one trusted believer. When you're ready, read "Busy Burial, Digital Doors, and Holy Rest" and "A Hard Word Softened by Grace." If you fail, get up. That's in the book too.

If you are in danger, or you are having thoughts of not wanting to live, please stop here and reach out now. In the U.S., call or text 988, or call 911. Then tell a pastor or a trusted believer today.

read.heading: Read first: Chapter 3
read.body:
Open to Chapter 3, "The Mandate of the Talents." Read "What Jesus Told Them" and "The One-Talent Excuse, and Comparison as a Shovel." Better yet, read the whole parable in your Bible first, Matthew 25:14-30, then the chapter.

Watch the third servant. He hands back exactly what he got. On paper it looks tidy. In Jesus' story, it's failure. Fear told him a story about his master, and then handed him a plan that felt responsible: hide it.

Then watch for comparison. It looks humble. But it can still put the Master's trust in the ground. Come back when you've read it.

prompts: What sentence about burial landed hardest?

pulse.heading: The pulse: trade it in love
pulse.body:
What God entrusts should be traded in love, not buried and labeled wisdom.

Carry Chapter 2 into this story. You don't multiply to be loved. You multiply because you're loved. And the reward isn't more pressure. Faithful servants enter their master's joy.

Notice the master says the same "well done" to the servant with less (Matthew 25:23). It's about faithfulness, not fame.

prompts: What does the master reward in this verse?

nameIt.heading: Name it: what's in the ground?
nameIt.body:
Chapter 3 lists what God entrusts: skills, time, influence, relationships, opportunities, spiritual gifts, resources, and the gospel itself. Look at that list slowly.

Now read the third servant's words. Fear told a false story about the master, and a wrong view of God made a wrong life. Jesus' warning at the end is serious. It is meant to wake us up, not to make God's children afraid of Him. If you belong to Christ, you know the Master the third servant never knew: holy, generous, and kind. Ask what story fear is telling you about Him.

And check for busy burial. You can bury a talent while looking busy: research forever, drafts never sent, apps organized for a calling you won't obey.

verses.text: He also who had received the one talent came forward, saying, ‘Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow, and gathering where you scattered no seed, so I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here, you have what is yours.’ But his master answered him, ‘You wicked and slothful servant! You knew that I reap where I have not sown and gather where I scattered no seed? Then you ought to have invested my money with the bankers, and at my coming I should have received what was my own with interest. So take the talent from him and give it to him who has the ten talents. For to everyone who has will more be given, and he will have an abundance. But from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away. And cast the worthless servant into the outer darkness. In that place there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.’

prompts: What gift, opportunity, or trust have I been protecting underground and calling wisdom?
What fear is hiding behind my caution? What story is it telling me about God?
Where am I burying something while looking busy?
Where am I confusing hustle metrics with faithfulness to the Master?

build.heading: Build it: one trade in seven days
build.body:
Name what you've buried and take one small step now. That's the whole chapter in one move.

A trade can be simple: serve, offer, start, give. One talent is enough to start. You don't need a five-talent story. You need a faithful step with what's in your hand.

move.heading: Move: this week's practice
move.body:
From the end of Chapter 3:

Name one buried talent in a single sentence. Take one concrete trade with it within seven days: serve, offer, start, or give. Tell one believer what you did.

If the week gets away from you, don't bury the plan too. Pick a new date within three days.

help.heading: Help: bring one answer, walk with one person
help.body:
Bring one answer to a trusted believer this week, and tell them what you traded.

Chapter 3 says start each day as a receiver and stay in community. So think of someone whose gift you've seen. Don't tell them what they're burying. Just tell them what you see God gave them, and thank God for it out loud.

pray.heading: Pray it
pray.body:
Start as a receiver. Then ask for courage.

Lord Jesus, my Master, everything I have came from You. You're not hard or harsh. You're generous, and You trusted me.

I've buried ____. Forgive me for calling fear wisdom.

Give me courage to trade with it this week by ____. Not to earn You. Because You already love me. If I fail, help me get up. Amen.

review.heading: Review: well done is about faithfulness
review.body:
After your date, mark it: traded, not yet, or holy wait.

Guardrail from Chapter 3: platforms are tools, not proof you're holy. Followers, views, and numbers aren't faithfulness. That's why nothing in this app counts your likes or ranks you. And "well done" isn't about fame. Hidden obedience counts. Quiet multiplication counts.

Faithful servants enter the Master's joy. Not more pressure. Joy.

You've walked three stops now. If something changed when you took your step, I'd love to hear it. Tap "Share what changed" from the menu.
